list.name: Changes
list.comment: The training data and the to_predict data passed to iai trees is now pd.DataFrames with categorical columns, as suggested by the IAI website.

task.summary: Default task

Improved the information presented for the pretty printing, but the explanations themselves are still to be improved. The next step is to make a ForcefulMannWhitneyU which tests on the best solutions of a Pref so that we can really check when a ps is good or bad on near-optimal solutions.
Implemented the forcefulMannWhitneyU test on near_optimal solutions, still to be tested.
Quality of life changes.
Added some checks to see if the explanations are actually correct or not.
Added functionality for the explanations to be stored individually into json files, and loaded from them.
Fixed various bugs.
Implemented the calendar change table for pss.
Implemented the range changes for a difference pattern, and now thinking about how to visualise a PS.
Implemented the linkage visualiser.
Fixed some bugs, isolated edges are a problem because they should be shown, but the layout doesn't know where to put them. Also, this causes stray edges?
Fixed a bug in how the labels were being placed in the plot, leaving some nodes without labels.
Last fixes of the day.
Small fixes
Quickly implemented the BTProblem.from_json so that it's replicable.
Made a clean script to generate the problem files.
Added to the script that the pRef is generated and then altered to match problem B.
Last fixes of the day.
Optima representation also includes the extra information now.
Implementing explanation storage by completely redoing the descriptors manager, oops. Still not completed and not tested.
the file generate_data_for_problem.py is close to being the final version of what will generate the data.
The final generate_data_for_problem.py file is complete and generates data that appears to be correct.
Added the hypothesis string to the explanations.
Added the explanation files to the repository, just in case.
Fixed a bug where the positive and negative p values were swapped around.
Workers are now listed in alphabetical order in the problem visualisation, solutions and pss.
Removed the name Penelope from the workers names because it's just too long
Penalty table for the optimal solution is now formatted in a way which makes it work immediately in the spreadsheets, although it it much less readable now...
Added a little additional call to generate an example problem which I can use to explain the problem
Rota numbers are also scrambled, but I'm not sure if they are being displayed correctly...

Fixed a quite serious bug, in which the rotas are not deterministic to how the pretty printer is created. Now, the rotas are first sorted by hash (instead of being converted from a set to a list) and then shuffled after setting a seed. The seed is calculated from the worker names.
End of day submit
The answers to the questions in the questionnaire are now generated.
Preparing for fairly big changes, clearing up code that was used for the LCS
In a frenzy, I implemented the variance based decision tree
Implemented some functionality for representation based search.
Played around with the variance decision tree again, seems to work nicely when paired with the perturbation metric.

Another manic episode, where i tried to implement many things that did not end up working. I think the safest approach is to have a representation of the solutions and search using variance but not perturbation linkage....
Fixing some issues in linkage methods, seeing that they are not that good....
Finally the tree looks right
Implemented the variance split linkage, and while it does kinda work, it's also not that good.
Implemented an objective which takes advatange that both mannwhitneyU and split variance are splitting the pRef.
More efficient metric evaluation
Cleaned up some code to split pRefs
Implemented an interface to make decision trees, and some simple functions to test them. For RR and a horrible ps budget given, the mse appears to be lower for my approach.
Final commit of the day
Implementing continuous problems
Implemented code which compares decision trees for many problems and depths.
Implemented the IAI trees, which are to be tuned so that nobody can complain
The training data and the to_predict data passed to iai trees is now pd.DataFrames with categorical columns, as suggested by the IAI website.
